Subject: Recap + sizing worksheet: dedicated capacity preference and TPS details

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated correctly. Attachment: BrightLine_expected_tps_worksheet.xlsx.

High-level notes from the call:
- BrightLine use case: synchronous clinician-facing summarization + batch analytics for compliance. Latency sensitive for the clinician UI (~95th %ile target discussed).
- Preferred deployment: you said "Dedicated capacity" with VPC peering if possible, and potential private control plane later on.
- Initial models: likely large open model family (70B-class) with 8-bit quantization preference, but you want Redwood recommendations.

Stuff we need from you to finalize sizing (worksheet attached):
1) Steady-state TPS target (avg requests/sec) and peak TPS (sustained/short burst).
2) Typical token mix: average prompt tokens, average generated tokens, % of short vs long sessions.
3) Concurrent active sessions target (typical number of simultaneous clinician requests during peak).
4) Latency SLO (p50/p95) and acceptable tail latency.

Next steps (proposed):
- You fill the worksheet and send back — Vivek will produce a recommended Dedicated sizing (GPU type, node counts, concurrency config, batch window, KV cache config) based on token mix.
- We schedule a 60-min technical workshop to walk through the recommendations and network/VPC details.
- I'll send a draft SOW to Procurement for review (attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf).

If anything above is wrong or missing, flag it. Otherwise, if you can complete the worksheet by EOD Tue 07/06 we can target a tech workshop the week of 07/13.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Recap + sizing worksheet: dedicated capacity preference and TPS details

Thanks Rafael — attached is a quick pass; I also pasted the key numbers below to save a round trip. We'll upload a filled worksheet by end of day.

Key numbers:
- Steady-state TPS (requests/sec): ~25 TPS (expected steady, clinician UI + some telemetry).
- Peak TPS: short bursts to 90 TPS (10-15 minute bursts during morning rounds).
- Token mix: average prompt = 120 tokens, average generation = 480 tokens -> average ~600 tokens per request.
- Request types: ~80% interactive (chat/summarization), 20% batch scoring.
- Concurrent active sessions at peak: target ~45 concurrent interactive requests.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300 ms for the interactive flows (we can tolerate up to 400 ms for complex cases).

Notes/questions:
- We want low variance in latency; if Dedicated needs significant warm-up for KV cache, flag it.
- Security: procurement asked whether we can do VPC peering + SOC2 evidence before contract final.

Sam

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@brightlinehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + sizing worksheet: dedicated capacity preference and TPS details

Thanks Sam — helpful numbers. Quick engineering read and follow-ups so we size nodes correctly:

Initial assumptions based on your token mix (600 tokens/request avg) and 90 TPS peak:
- Token throughput at peak = 90 req/sec * 600 tokens = 54k tokens/sec.
- For 95th < 300 ms, we should target low batch windows and aggressive KV/prefix caching for repeated clinician prompts.

GPU and node guidance (draft):
- Model family: 70B-class (we'll recommend an instruction-tuned variant). With 8-bit quantization and KV cache enabled we estimate ~40-55 tokens/sec per A100-80GB stream for interactive workloads. H100-80GB tends to give ~1.5x throughput for the same sequence lengths due to tensor core perf (and better mixed-precision ops).
- Suggested Dedicated starting point: 2 x H100-80GB nodes (or 3 x A100-80GB) in a reserved pool, with autoscaling/burst to 4 nodes for predictable morning bursts. This provides headroom for 90 TPS bursts while keeping steady-state cost reasonable.
- Concurrency config: enable 40-60 concurrent streams per node depending on multi-stream scheduler; we can tune continuous batching to keep p95 under 300 ms.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated patient-context lookups; this will reduce average tokens generated for repeated prompts and reduce latency.

Questions for Sam / procurement (technical):
1) Do you have a hard upper bound on monthly token consumption (billing/commit constraint)?
2) Network: are there fixed IPs for peering, and do you have an egress policy (we will need to confirm port/IP allow-lists)?
3) Any model constraints (no external downloads, air-gapped assets) that would push you to Private instead of Dedicated?

Action items I can take once we get confirmation:
- Produce a cost/throughput estimate comparing the two configurations (2xH100 vs 3xA100) and a fallback plan that pins to a smaller model variant during extreme load.
- Propose precise concurrency and batch window settings (we'll simulate using your token distributions from the worksheet).

Recommend scheduling a 60-min tech workshop (Vivek + infra + Sam + 1-2 of your engineers) to validate network/topology and run through SLOs. I can take the lead on the sizing doc and cost estimate.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (212) 555-0119

[Note: initial GPU guidance above is conservative; exact numbers depend on model variant, batch settings, and sequence-length distribution. We'll provide a more precise sims-based estimate in the next email.]
